items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: When you have Scott and Warren and Ralph and the guys, they’re all natural leaders.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you, you have a gift, and I’m going to kind of give a setting in which this gift manifests itself, and then I want you to talk about it. That is, not every musician, irregardless of their ability to be a great soloist or even to be a great arranger, has the gift to be a band leader, and you are a natural band leader. Talk about this.

That’s very interesting Mike, thank you. I say thank you because I enjoy being in control. I think that’s number one, you have to enjoy being in control. You have to really believe that the guys that you’re playing with will allow you to be in control and they won’t go kibbitzing around. But I think you have to be an extrovert, which is either you’re introvert or an extrovert, and you can’t do it halfheartedly, otherwise it fails. And the ability to conceive the beginning, the natural beginning of a tune and how…

what it’s probably about. You know, like how much time should you allow or allot a given piece? You know, for the most part though, like last night, well last night was not really a good example of what it was I can do as a leader because I was really not the leader I was more or less flung into it. When you have Scott and Warren and Ralph and the guys, they’re all natural leaders. Each of them wants to be the leader but they’re all being very reticent about taking the bull by the horns and doing it. But I prefer…
